script: diagnostic recorded from session: why CygOB2-C MIST R_V=3.5 alpha=2.0 regressed v4 -> v5
issue: #13 (new) — truth-age node set changes discontinuously under age-grid snapping
finding: The regression is NOT physical.  CygOB2-C's fitted age did not move at all (2.002 -> 2.002 Myr) and its extinction moved only -0.059 mag, but its 68% interval upper edge fell from 2.084 to 2.062 Myr.  That 0.022 Myr shift pushed a posterior quantile across a native-isochrone-age snapping boundary, DELETING the 2.248 Myr truth-age node that had carried 41.6% of the posterior weight in repair_v4.  The node set went from [1.783, 2.002, 2.248] to [1.783, 2.002], and bin 0's residual jumped +2.27 -> +3.25.
root_cause: The repair_v4 node rule snaps the nine posterior quantiles to native isochrone ages, whose grid is coarse (0.05 dex, about 12% in age).  An arbitrarily small change in the age posterior can therefore add or remove a whole node carrying tens of percent of the weight.  This is a cliff of exactly the same character as issue #11's Spearman p-value lattice: a coarse discretization making a continuous input produce a discontinuous output.
consequence: Re-specifying criterion R3 (issue #11) will NOT clear this cell, because this is not a threshold-boundary effect.  Two separate methodological fixes are needed before gate G3 can be re-evaluated fairly.
candidate_fix: Interpolate the truth isochrone between native ages instead of snapping, so the node set varies continuously with the posterior.  wp4_repair_common already does exactly this on the RECOVERY side (_interpolate_age_sequence), so the two sides are currently inconsistent: recovery interpolates, truth snaps.  Cost: the node count per branch would be fixed by the rule rather than by grid accidents, so injection cost is predictable.
not_a_reason_to_dismiss_the_cell: The cell genuinely fails at max|r| = 3.25 in the repair_v5 products as they stand, and must be reported under the section 13 retention policy regardless of cause.
